newsitem.title: PERU: Peru to set price in Luz del Sur shr sale on Dec 6.
newsitem.headline: Peru to set price in Luz del Sur shr sale on Dec 6.

text.p: Peruvian privatization officials said Monday they expected to set the price for the placement of the state's shares in electricity distributor Luz del Sur on December 6.
"It's December 6 because we expect the book-building abroad and at home to be finished a few days before this date," one privatization official, who asked not to be named, said in an interview.
The government holds a 30 percent stake in the electricity company, but has not formally specified what proportion of its shares it will sell.
It hopes to raise $200 million in total from the privatization.
Officials from investment bank CS First Boston, chosen by the government to handle the international portion of the sale, expect the placement abroad to raise about $100 million.
The domestic portion of the sale will be directed by local bank Banco Continental.

In the sale of shares to individual Peruvian nationals under the Citizens' Participation in Privatization scheme, Banco Continental will direct a group of local banks that includes Banco de Credito, Interbanc and Banco Wiese.

In the second part of the local sale, Spain's Banco Santander has been selected to handle the placement with local institutions. The Spanish bank's brokerage in Peru, Santander SAB, will direct a group of local brokerages to book-build with institutions such as local pension funds, insurance companies and banks.

In June 1994, a consortium consisting of Chile's Chilquinta International Inc and Canada's Ontario Hydro Inc bought a 60 percent stake in Luz del Sur, a former state-run electricity company for $212.1 million.
Another 10 percent stake is owned by the company's workers.
It will be the largest state share placement since July's $1.25 billion sale at home and abroad of a 26.6 percent state- held stake in Telefonica del Peru.
